chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya from Al-Amraki ibn Ali from Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) said:

I asked him about a man upon whom is the emancipation of a neck, and he intended to emancipate a person. Which of these two is better, if he emancipates an old man, or a beardless youth? He said: Emancipate the one who can be self-sufficient himself. The old weak sheikh is better than the beardless youth.
ai.seo_question: Which slave is better to free first: an old man or a young man?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS), the criterion for selecting a slave for manumission shifts from physical strength to the degree of self-sufficiency (ghina), establishing that freeing an elderly, dependent slave yields greater reward than freeing a young, robust one. This reflects the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on alleviating the burden of the most vulnerable, aligning with the principle that charity is most meritorious when directed toward those with the greatest need. The hadith thus recontextualizes the social value of the enslaved individual within the framework of spiritual merit.
